item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=PCFG-derived+uncertainty+metrics+as+triggers+for+meta-reasoning+loops+in+AI+architectures&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1007/bfb0013954\", \"title\": [\"Reasoning with uncertainty in AI\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/bfb0013954\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[1996]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/978-94-017-1743-4_3\", \"title\": [\"Temporal Semantics of Meta-Level Architectures for Dynamic Control of Reasoning\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/978-94-017-1743-4_3\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2001]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6759126\", \"title\": [\"An Engineering Framework for Self-Correcting Autonomous AI Agents: Mitigating Hallucinations and Reasoning Loops in Autonomous Engineering Workflows\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This paper presents TRACE (Trajectory Reliability and Correction Engine), a runtime self-correction framework for autonomous AI agents in engineering workflows. TRACE targets a reliability gap in multi-step tool-using agents, where unsupported claims, contradictions, repetitive loops, and tool-use anomalies can propagate across long execution trajectories. Existing self-correction methods typically rely on post-hoc reflection or a single intervention mechanism, but do not integrate continuous runtime monitoring, failure attribution, and adaptive recovery in one control layer. TRACE wraps a standard ReAct-style agent with four modules: a Trajectory Monitor, a Failure Attribution module, a Recovery Controller, and an Audit Layer for structured trace logging. We evaluate TRACE on a simulated enterprise incident-triage benchmark of 50 tasks with injected hallucination- and loop-inducing conditions across four difficulty levels. TRACE achieves 76.0% task success versus 68.0% for a self-reflection baseline and 62.0% for vanilla ReAct, while reducing hallucination incidence from 19.4% to 9.6% and loop frequency from 12.1% to 4.8%. The framework is intended for reliable, auditable autonomous execution in engineering environments.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6759126\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.5226493\", \"title\": [\"Synthetic reasoning - Designing AI Architectures Beyond N…
